paragraphs.text: Reference is invited to circular GZ-KYC-2019-01 dated April 15, 2019 on Customer Due Diligence. Where the customer is a legal person or arrangement, banks shall identify the beneficial owner, being the natural person who ultimately owns or controls the customer, using the thresholds specified in this circular.

Beneficial ownership threshold for companies: where the customer is a company, the beneficial owner shall be the natural person who, alone or together with others, has a controlling ownership interest of more than 10 percent of the shares, capital or profits of the company, or who exercises control through other means.

Beneficial ownership threshold for partnership firms: where the customer is a partnership firm, the beneficial owner shall be the natural person who, alone or together with others, has ownership of or entitlement to more than 15 percent of the capital or profits of the partnership firm.

Beneficial ownership threshold for unincorporated associations: where the customer is an unincorporated association or body of individuals, the beneficial owner shall be the natural person who, alone or together with others, has ownership of or entitlement to more than 15 percent of the property, capital or profits of the association.

Beneficial ownership for trusts: where the customer is a trust, the beneficial owners shall include the author of the trust, the trustees, the beneficiaries with 10 percent or more interest in the trust, and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control over the trust.

Senior managing official as beneficial owner: where no natural person is identified as beneficial owner of a company, partnership firm or association under the applicable threshold, the bank shall treat the natural person holding the position of senior managing official as the beneficial owner. These provisions are effective from March 1, 2021.
